name: numbers
why: Without this a port passes with an emitter that writes 0.0 for integer 0 and 1.6716E-5 for 0.000016716 — Jackson round-trips the base fixture byte-perfectly while doing exactly that (spikes/classifier/reports/99-verdict.md §3). The request numbers live in state, which is outside the byte claim, so the assertion here is on the PARSE: every value below must come back numerically equal, and a zero probability must stay a zero, not become absent.

is_expensive.instructions: Is this operation expensive relative to a typical request?

expect.notes: Compare numerically, never as strings: 0 vs 0.0 and 1.6716e-5 vs 0.000016716 are the same value and different bytes. A port that types the probability map as a float and prints 0.0 for 0 still passes THIS fixture and fails the wire — which is why the canonical bytes are asserted separately, on model + questions.
